title: Model & Config-Sensitive Structured Output Regression Detector
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a detector that correlates structured-output (JSON/schema) regressions specifically to model and config deltas so rollouts can be automatically triaged and mitigated.

Problem context: We observe intermittent schema violations (missing fields, type mismatches, unexpected enum values) after model upgrades or when serving configs (beam_size, sampling temperature, prompt templating, kv-cache settings) change. Current monitors surface aggregate drift but do not attribute to specific config/model slices or generate actionable remediation steps.

Scope:
- Create per-slice evaluators keyed by (model_version, config_hash, route, sample-cohort) that compute a Field Fragility Score (FFS) for each schema field.
- Run both offline batch comparison (pre-rollout shadow) and lightweight online sampling during canaries.
- Support synthetic schema fuzzing to enumerate borderline cases (truncated arrays, null vs empty string, nested object flattening).
- Provide thresholds and hysteresis for alerting and an automatic rollback trigger policy for high-severity regressions.

Design highlights:
- Field Fragility Score (FFS): combines three signals (violation_rate, severity_weight, change_amplification) into a single per-field metric to prioritize alerts.
- Config-slice delta engine: computes asymmetric deltas when comparing baseline and candidate model/config pairs; reports which config knobs correlate strongly with regression signals.
- Canary integration: light-weight sample budget per route; if FFS exceeds threshold for critical fields, mark canary as FAILED and optionally trigger model fallback defined in rollout policy.
- Observability: new per-field timeseries in Console, histogram of violation types, and a ranked table of top contributing config keys.

Deliverables:
- Evaluation microservice (stateless) exposing /evaluate-slice and /compare-pair APIs for batch and streaming ingestion.
- Canary hook in rollout controller that queries the microservice and emits canary decisions.
- Console pages: FFS dashboard, per-release regressor report, and suggested remediation checklist.
- Automation: an incident playbook stub and GitHub PR template for rollbacks when triggered.

Acceptance criteria:
1) FFS computed for at least 80% of schema fields across three representative product routes.
2) Canary integration successfully flags a synthetic regression in internal testbed and blocks rollout in 2/2 runs.
3) Console surfaces field-level root-cause and the top 3 correlated config knobs.
4) Documentation and playbook published in Confluence and linked from the Console.
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting - agreed to use a hybrid approach (offline shadow vs online lightweight canary). Diego to spike FFS formula with historical logs.
2026-03-04: Spike complete - early FFS prototype shows good separation for missing-field vs type-coercion errors. Added synthetic fuzz test harness to cover edge cases.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and UX. Console mockups accepted with minor layout changes. Decided to surface 'top 3 contributing config knobs' using mutual information metric.
2026-03-10: Engineering started implementing batch compare API. Integration ticket with rollout controller created. Added ENG-58722 as follow-up for performance optimization of streaming path.
